headline: Aerospace strength lifts margins, raises full-year outlook
summary_short: ATI's Q2 2026 revenue rose 10.6% y/y to $1,261M, above the high end of its own guidance, with operating income up 36.6% y/y to $220M and diluted EPS up 55.7% y/y to $1.09, while the company raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA, EPS, and free-cash-flow guidance.
summary_long: Revenue rose 10.6% y/y to $1,261M, driven by a 13% rise in aerospace & defense sales (commercial jet engines +10% y/y, defense +90% y/y). Gross profit rose 27.8% y/y to $310M and operating income rose 36.6% y/y to $220M; adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 440bp y/y to 22.6%. GAAP diluted EPS rose 55.7% y/y to $1.09 (adjusted EPS $1.23, +66% y/y), including a $9.9M gain on an AA&S facility sale. Cash rose to $783M after $450M of new senior notes; the company repurchased $50M of stock. ATI raised FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $1,135M-$1,185M (from $1,010M-$1,060M), adjusted EPS to $4.90-$5.18 (from $4.20-$4.48), and adjusted free cash flow to $550M-$600M (from $465M-$525M), citing pricing, mix, and rising capacity.

drivers.explanation: Sales rose 11% y/y (per the release) driven by a 13% increase in aerospace & defense sales; within that, commercial jet engine sales rose 10% y/y and defense sales rose 90% y/y on higher demand and pricing.

Not explained directly at the consolidated level; HPMC segment EBITDA margin rose 40bp y/y to 24.1% on higher volume and favorable jet-engine pricing, and AA&S segment EBITDA margin rose 930bp y/y to 23.7% on higher pricing and mix plus a one-time gain.

AA&S segment EBITDA rose to $147.6M (23.7% of sales), including a $9.9M gain on the sale of a closed manufacturing facility plus higher pricing and favorable mix; HPMC segment EBITDA rose to $153.5M on higher volume and favorable jet-engine nickel pricing, partly offset by higher manufacturing and period costs.

Includes a $9.9 million ($0.06/share) gain from the sale of a previously closed AA&S manufacturing facility; special items (start-up/transaction, transformation, restructuring costs, and AR-sale losses) reduced net income by $18.7 million after tax in the quarter.
Follows net income growth of 50% y/y; diluted share count fell slightly to 138.3M from 143.1M y/y aided by $50M of quarterly buybacks, and the $9.9M asset-sale gain added $0.06 per share.

Cash rose to $783.0 million driven by $450 million of senior notes proceeds and $223.4 million of net financing inflow year-to-date, partly offset by $125.0 million of treasury stock purchases; the quarter itself generated $131.8 million of operating cash flow.

Management cites results above the high end of Q2 guidance, 37% y/y adjusted EBITDA growth on 11% sales growth, a record $4.4 billion backlog (+18% y/y), and continued portfolio shift toward higher-margin aerospace, defense and specialty energy exposure supporting the raised full-year outlook.
